trust_decision.summary: Which on-disk files under the user's selected share/website folders may be served to anonymous web visitors; decided when the file inventory is built (set_file_info walk, build_zipfile_list, ZipWriter) and when a request streams a file. At the pinned commit nothing resolves symlinks against the selected roots.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'follows symlinks in shared directories'. The obvious place to look is the os.walk over shared directories that builds self.files, which both share and website modes use.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: ZipWriter.add_dir already skips symlinks (share_mode.py:595), and ZipWriter is a generic archiver that also works without a web object, so a solver can argue it is safe or not part of the HTTP serving path. The single-file /download branch (share_mode.py:492-505) looks like 'the user picked exactly this file' rather than a directory walk.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Sharing a mix of explicitly selected files and folders, e.g. `onionshare a.txt dir/`, plus ordinary nested regular files, must keep working. The published containment check only records directories as roots (fix.diff:13-17), so a root-level regular file outside every selected dir fails _is_path_contained (fix.diff:31-34, fix.diff:195-197) and is dropped. That is an over-broad breakage in the published fix itself. Explicitly passed symlink arguments are also silently dropped (fix.diff:26-28).

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer adding 'serve index.html from any listed dir' would naturally join the filesystem path, bypassing the filtered inventory.
